title: Grateful Dead Live at Seattle Center Arena on 1973-06-26

ai_review.summary: Patchy matrix source but an energetic 1973 show that shines on China Cat Sunflower, The Other One/Bobby McGee and the Truckin'‑Drums‑Too sandwich.
ai_review.review: The performance is generally high‑energy with many fans highlighting the powerful China Cat > Rider stretch, a soaring Box/You Ain't Woman Enough vocal blend, and the classic Truckin' → Drums → Too sequence. The recording is a mixed soundboard/audience patch that suffers from occasional dropouts, channel swaps and pitch quirks, making the listening experience uneven despite moments of crisp clarity.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (≈4/5) while noting significant but not fatal recording issues (≈3/5); weighted combination yields a solid mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Patchwork of soundboard and audience sources leads to inconsistent clarity; brief dropouts in Truckin' and Black Peter, occasional channel swaps and pitch adjustments are noted. Overall listenable but not consistently clean.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
The Other One (with Bobby McGee segue)
poor_songs: Jack Straw (as noted by one reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Both sets flow well, with the first set building energy through strong vocal harmonies and the second set delivering a classic Truckin'‑Drums‑Too climax; occasional patch transitions are audible but do not break overall momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is solid, though several reviewers note he fades into the background during China Cat Sunflower.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil delivers monster bass lines, especially on He's Gone and Bertha, earning high praise throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir shines with aggressive rhythm playing and takes lead vocals on multiple numbers, most notably delivering a standout performance on China Cat Sunflower.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith provides lively intros and generally solid keyboard work, though one reviewer described occasional kludgy moments.
